answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The fable holds work receipts rather than names, so the river of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on reputation decay for idle identities, reset on any identity-link attempt, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. The lantern of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
